description: Surfaced by the fz-usm investigation (2026-07-05). resolve.rs:212 resolves TypeExpr::EmptyList ([]) to types.nil(), but types.empty_list() (types/mod.rs:423-425) exists and is used elsewhere (world_test.rs:281). Is [] in TYPE position meant to be the nil atom or the empty-list type? Orthogonal to fz-usm's constructor registry (this is list-type semantics, not constructor resolution). Investigate intent; likely should be empty_list(). Small.

comments.text: DONE (folded to a5b44bf54). TypeExpr::EmptyList ([] in type position) now resolves to empty_list() (list axis, ValueKind LIST) not nil() (atom axis, ValueKind ATOM). Evidence: Elixir typespec parity ([]=empty list, nil=atom); GroundValue::Nil vs EmptyList already distinct at value level; empty_list() already existed; no prior test asserted the old behavior. Intent-stating test added (empty_list_brackets_resolve_to_the_empty_list_type_not_nil). Self-audited: sole TypeExpr::EmptyList site, clean intent comment (no ticket ID). Scoped strictly to type position; broader fz-iib (nil-as-atom expr vs empty-list pattern) left untouched. lib 1229/0/9; single-threaded fixture_matrix 19 unchanged.

title: TypeExpr::EmptyList ([] in type position) resolves to nil() not empty_list()
